meaning: Megachasma, Greek mégas “big” + cháskō “yawning hole or open mouth”, referring to its unusually large oral cavity; pelagios, Greek pelágios “of the sea”, referring to its oceanic, epipelagic habitat
description: A soft, flabby filter feeder with a huge mouth at the tip of a broad, rounded snout, rimmed by a pale band on the upper jaw. It swims slowly with its mouth open to strain krill and other plankton, and its tail has a long upper lobe. The back is dark grey-brown to blackish, and it was first found in 1976, when one came up tangled in a ship's sea anchor off Hawaii.
depth: Surface to about 1,200 m, deeper by day and shallower at night
